commands.review_summary:
The PR resolves sub-1024 legacy Anthropic thinking budgets as disabled in the direct provider and agent transport option-resolution paths, swaps legacy payload fallbacks from `||` to `??`, and adds regression tests for both builders.

PR surface: Source +6, Tests +98. Total +104 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection on current main shows legacy Anthropic budget resolution can collapse below 1024, and the Anthropic SDK contract rejects enabled budgets below that minimum; I did not run a live Anthropic call in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Manual review is needed because the PR has a blocking raw-entry correctness finding and contributor-side real behavior proof is still required before merge.

target.title: fix(anthropic): resolve thinking as disabled when legacy budget is below 1024
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `adjustMaxTokensForThinking` collapses the legacy thinking budget below the Anthropic minimum (1024 tokens) — either to zero or a sub-minimum positive value — the option resolution layer unconditionally sets `thinkingEnabled: true`. This creates two bugs:

1. **`||` overrides explicit zero to 1024**: `options?.thinkingBudgetTokens || 1024` treats zero as falsy, silently substituting 1024 tokens the caller never requested.
2. **Sub-minimum budgets reach the API**: A computed budget of e.g. 476 tokens is emitted as `{ type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 476 }`, which the Anthropic API rejects (contract: `budget_tokens >= 1024`).

Both bugs happen in the direct provider and the agent transport stream — the two builders share the same pattern.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix normalises state at **option resolution** — the layer where `thinkingEnabled` and `thinkingBudgetTokens` are decided — rather than patching at payload construction. When `adjusted.thinkingBudget < 1024`, the resolution sets `thinkingEnabled: false` so **every downstream consumer** sees the same closed state:

- **Payload builder** → emits `{ type: "disabled" }` (explicit, API-valid)
- **Temperature** → `!thinkingEnabled` passes through custom temperature values
- **Replay** → `replayThinkingEnabled` stays `false`, no stale content filtering
- **Tool-choice** → `normalizeAnthropicToolChoice` receives the correct flag

The `||` → `??` change in both builders is defensive hygiene; the resolution layer already prevents invalid budgets from reaching the builder through the normal code path.

This directly addresses the feedback on [closed PR #101283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101283), where the same bug was fixed at the payload layer instead — silently omitting the `thinking` block while `thinkingEnabled` remained `true`, leaving replay, temperature, and tool-choice internally inconsistent.

## User Impact

Callers whose model context window is too small to fit the selected reasoning level no longer get:
- A silently inflated 1024-token thinking budget (the `||` override)
- An API-rejected request with a sub-minimum `budget_tokens` value

Instead thinking is explicitly disabled with `{ type: "disabled" }`, matching the API contract and keeping all internal state consistent.

## Evidence

**After fix — 65 + 102 tests pass:**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts --run
Tests  65 passed (65)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts --run
Tests  102 passed (102)
```

**Negative control — same tests against `origin/main` (4 new tests fail):**

```
Provider:
  FAIL  resolves thinking as disabled when the legacy budget collapses below 1024
        Expected: { type: "disabled" }
        Received: { type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 1024 }   ← || overrode 0

  FAIL  resolves thinking as disabled when the legacy budget is positive but sub-minimum
        Expected: { type: "disabled" }
        Received: { type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 476 }    ← API would reject

Transport:
  FAIL  resolves thinking as disabled when the legacy budget collapses to zero
        Expected: { type: "disabled" }
        Received: { type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 1024 }   ← same bug

  FAIL  resolves thinking as disabled when the legacy budget is positive but sub-minimum
        Expected: { type: "disabled" }
        Received: { type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 476 }    ← same bug
```

**Test coverage (4 new tests across both builders):**

| Scenario | Provider | Transport |
|----------|----------|-----------|
| Budget zero (1024-token model, minimal reasoning) | `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` | `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` |
| Budget sub-minimum (1500-token model, low reasoning → 476) | `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` | `thinking: { type: "disabled" }` |
| Normal budget (existing tests unchanged) | `thinking: { type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N }` | same |

**Format:** `oxfmt` clean on all 4 changed files.
